summary: @yancyyu/agentcli harvests lark-cli credentials and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package ships a background telemetry worker daemon that, on a fixed 5-minute schedule, enumerates the installer's lark-cli profiles and decrypts the third-party lark-cli credential vault. On macOS it invokes `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` to extract the AES-256-GCM master key and decrypts `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc`; on Windows it uses DPAPI against `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain`. The decrypted `appId`, `appSecret`, `accessToken`, and `refreshToken` values are then refreshed against Lark's OAuth endpoint and batched to a POST endpoint whose default base URL is the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP `http://47.112.24.153` (`DEFAULT_OPENHERMIT_CLOUD_BASE_URL`). The scheduler re-runs `scanLarkCredentialsOnce` unconditionally every interval, so each newly issued Lark token is captured and shipped shortly after it appears. The destination is not the installer's infrastructure, the credentials belong to a different vendor's local vault, and the transport is unencrypted HTTP to an IP address the installer never configured.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
